items.title: A Dead Phone
items.text:
Jian: Owen, do you have a phone charger? Mine is at home.
Owen: Yes, I have one in my bag. Do you need it right now?
Jian: Only during lunch. My phone is almost dead, and I must call home after school.
Owen: No problem. But the plug in our classroom is far from the desks.
Jian: I could sit on the floor near the wall. Would that be all right?
Owen: Sure. Actually, why don't you use the one in the library? It is quieter there.
Jian: Good idea! Can I borrow your charger, though? The library has no cables.
Owen: Of course. Just bring it back before the last class. I need it on the bus.
Jian: I promise. You saved my day!
Owen: Anytime. Remember to unplug it.

qs.q: Why does Jian need the charger?
o: To play a game at lunch
qs.why: Jian은 'I must call home after school'라고 말해요. 그래서 방과 후 집에 전화하려고 충전기가 필요해요.

qs.q: Where will Jian probably charge the phone?
qs.why: Owen이 도서관을 제안하고 Jian이 '도서관에는 케이블이 없다'며 충전기를 빌려 달라고 해요. 그래서 도서관에서 충전할 가능성이 높아요.

qs.q: What does "You saved my day" mean?
o: You helped me at an important time
You gave me extra free time
You taught me a new lesson
qs.why: 'save my day'는 곤란한 순간에 도움을 받아 하루가 잘 풀리게 되었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Owen say, "Why don't you use the one in the library?"
qs.why: 'Why don't you ~?'는 제안할 때 쓰는 표현이에요. 더 조용한 도서관을 권하는 거예요.

qs.q: What will Jian probably do before the last class?
o: Give the charger back to Owen
Ask the teacher for a cable
qs.why: Owen이 마지막 수업 전에 돌려 달라고 했고 Jian이 약속한다고 했어요. 그래서 충전기를 돌려줄 거예요.

items.title: Too Loud at Night
items.text:
Dara: Hi, Hyun. Do you have a minute?
Hyun: Sure, Dara. What's up?
Dara: It's about the music last night. I could hear it through the wall until after midnight.
Hyun: Oh no, I'm so sorry. I didn't know it was that loud.
Dara: I understand you were having fun. But I have an important exam today, and I could hardly sleep.
Hyun: That's fair. From now on, I'll use headphones after ten o'clock.
Dara: Thank you. That would help a lot.
Hyun: And if it's ever too loud again, please knock on my door.
Dara: I will. Thanks for being so understanding.
Hyun: No problem. Good luck today!

qs.q: Until what time could Dara hear the music?
qs.why: Dara는 'until after midnight', 즉 자정이 넘을 때까지 음악이 들렸다고 말해요.

qs.q: How does Hyun probably feel after hearing the complaint?
qs.why: Hyun은 'I'm so sorry'라고 사과하고 앞으로 헤드폰을 쓰겠다고 해요. 미안해하는 마음이에요.

qs.q: What does Hyun mean by "That's fair"?
o: Both rooms are the same size
qs.why: 'That's fair'는 상대의 말이 공정하고 합당하다고 인정할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

qs.q: Why does Dara begin with "Do you have a minute?"
o: To invite Hyun to a party
To ask Hyun for time to talk
To ask what time it is
qs.why: 'Do you have a minute?'은 잠깐 이야기할 시간이 있는지 정중하게 묻는 말이에요. 불편한 이야기를 꺼내기 위한 시작이에요.

qs.q: What will Dara probably do if the noise happens again?
qs.why: Hyun이 'please knock on my door'라고 부탁했고 Dara가 'I will'이라고 답해요.

items.title: A Late Library Book
items.text:
Eun: Excuse me, the computer says I have a late book, but I returned mine on Monday.
Ms. Cho: Let me check. Which book is it?
Eun: It's about space travel. The title is Journey to Mars.
Ms. Cho: I see the problem. You returned Journey to Mars. The late book is Journey to the Moon.
Eun: Oh! I borrowed two books with similar names. Maybe I forgot the second one.
Ms. Cho: That's possible. Could you check your bag?
Eun: Wait... here it is! It was under my notebook. I'm so embarrassed.
Ms. Cho: Don't worry. It happens a lot. The fine is two hundred won a day, and it's been three days.
Eun: Here is the money. I'll be more careful next time.
Ms. Cho: Thank you. You can borrow new books now.

qs.q: Which book was late?
qs.why: Ms. Cho는 'The late book is Journey to the Moon'이라고 말해요.

qs.q: What caused the misunderstanding?
o: Eun gave the book to a friend
qs.why: Eun이 'I borrowed two books with similar names'라고 말해요. 제목이 비슷한 두 권 때문에 혼동이 생겼어요.

qs.q: What does "I'm so embarrassed" mean?
o: Eun is too busy to talk
Eun is angry at the librarian
Eun feels ashamed of the mistake
qs.why: 'embarrassed'는 실수 때문에 부끄럽고 민망한 감정을 나타내요.

qs.q: Why does Ms. Cho say, "Don't worry. It happens a lot"?
o: To warn Eun about a rule
qs.why: 흔한 일이라고 말해서 Eun을 안심시키려는 의도예요.

qs.q: What will Eun probably do after the talk?
o: Search for the Mars book again
Look for another book to borrow
Buy a new copy of the book
qs.why: Ms. Cho가 'You can borrow new books now'라고 했으므로 새 책을 빌릴 가능성이 높아요.

items.title: Surprise Party Plans
items.text:
Mina: Joon, Dana's birthday is next Friday. Let's plan a surprise party.
Joon: Great idea! Where should we have it?
Mina: How about the school garden after class? It's free, and Dana loves flowers.
Joon: Hmm, I'm not sure. The weather might be cold by then. What about the music room?
Mina: Good point. I'll ask Mr. Oh if we can use it.
Joon: I can bring the cake. My aunt owns a bakery.
Mina: Wonderful! I'll make invitations and ask everyone to keep it secret.
Joon: But how do we get Dana to the room?
Mina: I'll say that a teacher wants to see Dana after school. Dana won't suspect anything.
Joon: Perfect. Let's meet at lunch tomorrow to finalize the details.

qs.q: Why does Joon disagree with the school garden?
qs.why: Joon은 'The weather might be cold by then'라며 정원에 반대해요.

qs.q: What can we guess about Joon's aunt?
qs.why: Joon은 이모가 빵집을 운영하니 케이크를 가져올 수 있다고 말해요. 그래서 빵이나 케이크를 만드는 일과 관련이 있어요.

qs.q: What does "finalize the details" mean?
qs.why: 'finalize'는 마무리하다, 확정하다라는 뜻이에요. 세부 사항을 최종 결정한다는 의미예요.

qs.q: Why does Joon say, "Hmm, I'm not sure"?
o: To say sorry for being late
To politely disagree with the idea
To change the date of the party
qs.why: 'I'm not sure'는 직접 반대하지 않고 공손하게 의견이 다르다는 것을 나타내요.

qs.q: What will the two friends probably do tomorrow?
o: Finish the party plans at lunch
Hold the party in the garden
qs.why: Joon이 'Let's meet at lunch tomorrow'라고 했어요. 내일 점심에 만나 계획을 마무리해요.

items.title: Choosing a Project
items.text:
Sua: Theo, we must choose a project for the science fair. What do you think about the plant growth test?
Theo: Honestly, it takes too long. Plants need weeks to grow, and the fair is in ten days.
Sua: True. Then how about testing which paper towel absorbs the most water?
Theo: That sounds easier, but I'm worried it's a little boring.
Sua: In my opinion, boring is fine if the results are clear. Judges like clear results.
Theo: Hmm, you may be right. Could we add a chart to show the results?
Sua: Definitely. I can draw it on a big poster.
Theo: Then I'm in. I'll buy three kinds of paper towels this afternoon.
Sua: Great! I'll write down the steps so we do not forget anything.

qs.q: Why does Theo reject the plant growth test?
qs.why: Theo는 식물이 자라는 데 몇 주가 걸리는데 대회는 10일 뒤라고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the paper towel test?
qs.why: 대회까지 10일뿐인데 Theo가 이 실험은 더 쉽다고 하고 재료만 사면 되므로 짧은 시간에 끝낼 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "I'm in" mean?
o: I agree to join the plan
qs.why: 'I'm in'은 계획에 참여하겠다는 구어체 표현이에요.

qs.q: Why does Sua say, "Judges like clear results"?
o: To persuade Theo that the idea is good
qs.why: Sua는 심사위원이 명확한 결과를 좋아한다는 근거로 Theo를 설득하려고 해요.

qs.q: What will Theo probably do this afternoon?
qs.why: Theo가 'I'll buy three kinds of paper towels this afternoon'이라고 말해요.

items.title: Carrying Boxes
items.text:
Yuna: Excuse me, those boxes look heavy. Do you need a hand?
Lim: Oh, that would be wonderful. They are full of canned food for the food drive.
Yuna: Where should I put them?
Lim: In the hall on the second floor. The elevator is broken, I'm afraid.
Yuna: That's okay. I can carry two at a time.
Lim: You're very kind. By the way, are you a volunteer here?
Yuna: Not yet. I just came to drop off some soup cans from my family.
Lim: How thoughtful! We still need helpers on Saturdays, if you're interested.
Yuna: I'd love to, but I have to check my schedule first.
Lim: No rush. Take this flyer, and call the number when you decide.

qs.q: Why will Yuna use the stairs?
o: The hall is on the first floor
qs.why: Lim이 'The elevator is broken'이라고 말해서 계단으로 옮겨야 해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Yuna?
qs.why: Yuna는 아직 자원봉사자는 아니지만 'I'd love to'라고 하며 일정만 확인하면 돼요.

qs.q: What does "I'm afraid" mean in "The elevator is broken, I'm afraid"?
qs.why: 문장 끝의 'I'm afraid'는 안 좋은 소식을 정중하게 전할 때 쓰며 '유감이지만'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Lim give Yuna a flyer?
o: So Yuna can see a map
So Yuna can learn how to volunteer
So Yuna can find the elevator
qs.why: Lim은 전단지를 주며 결정하면 전화하라고 해요. 자원봉사 안내 정보를 주려는 거예요.

qs.q: What will Yuna probably do after checking the schedule?
o: Call the number on the flyer
qs.why: Lim이 결정하면 전단지의 번호로 전화하라고 했어요.

items.title: The Wrong Time
items.text:
Hana: Jun, where are you? The movie starts in ten minutes!
Jun: What? I thought we were having dinner first and seeing the movie later.
Hana: No, my message said, "Let's see the five o'clock show."
Jun: Oh, I see. I read it too quickly. I'm really sorry for the confusion.
Hana: It's okay, but I've been waiting at the ticket counter for twenty minutes.
Jun: I'm on the bus now. I can get there in fifteen minutes.
Hana: Then you'll miss the beginning. Why don't we change to the seven o'clock show?
Jun: That sounds good. Shall I buy the tickets online right now?
Hana: Yes, please. In the meantime, I'll find a place for dinner nearby.
Jun: Great. See you soon!

qs.q: How long has Hana been waiting?
qs.why: Hana는 'I've been waiting ... for twenty minutes'라고 말해요.

qs.q: What caused the misunderstanding?
qs.why: Jun이 'I read it too quickly'라고 인정해요. 메시지를 잘못 이해해 저녁을 먼저 먹는다고 생각했어요.

qs.q: What does "In the meantime" mean?
qs.why: 'in the meantime'은 그동안, 그사이에라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Hana say, "Why don't we change to the seven o'clock show?"
qs.why: 'Why don't we ~?'로 해결책을 제안해요. Jun이 5시 상영을 못 보게 되었기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What will Jun probably do next?
qs.why: Jun이 'Shall I buy the tickets online?'라고 물었고 Hana가 'Yes, please'라고 답해요.

items.title: A Shirt That Shrank
items.text:
Bora: Excuse me, I bought this shirt last week, but it shrank after one wash.
Clerk: I'm sorry to hear that. Did you follow the washing instructions?
Bora: Yes, I washed it in cold water, just like the label says.
Clerk: May I see the label? Hmm, you're right. That shouldn't happen.
Bora: I don't want to be difficult, but I'd like to exchange it.
Clerk: Of course. Do you have your receipt?
Bora: Here it is. Do you have the same shirt in a larger size?
Clerk: Let me check the storeroom. It will take about five minutes.
Bora: No problem. I'll look at the jackets over there while I wait.
Clerk: Thank you for your patience.

qs.q: How did Bora wash the shirt?
qs.why: Bora는 'I washed it in cold water'라고 말해요.

qs.q: Why does the Clerk ask to see the label?
qs.why: 점원은 먼저 세탁 방법을 지켰는지 물었고 라벨을 보고 'you're right'라고 인정해요.

qs.q: Why does Bora say, "I don't want to be difficult, but..."?
qs.why: 이 표현은 까다롭게 굴려는 것이 아니라는 뜻으로 요구나 불만을 정중하게 꺼낼 때 써요.

qs.q: What does "patience" mean in "Thank you for your patience"?
qs.why: 'patience'는 짜증 내지 않고 기다리는 인내심을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What will the Clerk probably do next?
o: Ask Bora to come back next week
qs.why: 점원이 'Let me check the storeroom'이라고 말해요.

items.title: Park Clean-Up Day
items.text:
Ara: Dohyun, are you coming to the park clean-up this Saturday?
Dohyun: I'd like to, but what time does it start?
Ara: At nine. We meet by the fountain, and the city gives us gloves and bags.
Dohyun: Good. Do I need to bring anything?
Ara: Just water and a hat. It might be sunny.
Dohyun: Got it. Can I invite my little sister? She's ten.
Ara: Hmm, I think that's fine as long as an adult is with her.
Dohyun: My dad can come too. He loves working outdoors.
Ara: Even better! The more people we have, the faster we'll finish.
Dohyun: Then I'll tell them tonight and see you at nine.

qs.q: What should Dohyun bring?
qs.why: Ara는 'Just water and a hat'이라고 말해요. 장갑과 봉투는 시에서 줘요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about young children at the clean-up?
o: They need an adult with them
They can come only at noon
qs.why: Ara는 'as long as an adult is with her'라고 조건을 붙여요. 어린 아이는 어른과 함께 와야 해요.

qs.q: What does "as long as" mean in "as long as an adult is with her"?
qs.why: 'as long as'는 '~하기만 하면'이라는 조건을 나타내요.

qs.q: Why does Ara say, "Even better!"?
o: She is happy more people will come
qs.why: 아버지도 올 수 있다는 말에 사람이 많을수록 좋다고 기뻐하는 거예요.

qs.q: What will Dohyun probably do tonight?
o: Ask his sister and dad to come
qs.why: Dohyun은 'I'll tell them tonight'라고 말해요. 여기서 them은 여동생과 아버지예요.

items.title: Changing Seats
items.text:
Nari: Excuse me, may I ask you something?
Teacher: Of course, Nari. What is it?
Nari: I'm sitting in the back row, and I can't read the board clearly.
Teacher: Have you had your eyes checked recently?
Nari: Not for two years. My parents are making an appointment this week.
Teacher: Good. Until then, would you like to move to the front?
Nari: Yes, please. But I don't want anyone to feel upset.
Teacher: Don't worry. Seiha wants to sit near the window in the back, so you two can switch.
Nari: That works perfectly. Thank you so much.
Teacher: You're welcome. Let me know if it gets better after you see the doctor.

qs.q: How long has it been since Nari's last eye check?
qs.why: Nari는 'Not for two years'라고 답해요.

qs.q: Why does the Teacher ask about Nari's eyes?
o: Poor eyesight may be the problem
qs.why: 칠판이 잘 안 보인다는 말에 시력 문제일 수 있다고 생각해 눈 검사를 받았는지 물어요.

qs.q: What does "That works perfectly" mean?
qs.why: 'work'는 '효과가 있다, 잘 맞는다'는 뜻이에요. 좌석을 바꾸는 방법이 딱 알맞다는 말이에요.

qs.q: Why does Nari say, "I don't want anyone to feel upset"?
o: Nari wants to stay in the back
Nari is afraid of the teacher
qs.why: 다른 학생이 기분 상하지 않기를 바란다는 말에서 배려하는 마음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What will probably happen next in class?
o: Nari and Seiha will switch seats
The teacher will move the board
qs.why: 교사가 Seiha와 자리를 바꾸자고 했고 Nari가 좋다고 답해요.

items.title: The Wrong Drink
items.text:
Customer: Excuse me, I ordered a hot chocolate, but this looks like coffee.
Server: Oh, I'm sorry. Let me check the order. You're right. The note says "hot chocolate." My mistake.
Customer: It's fine, but I'm in a bit of a hurry. My bus leaves in twelve minutes.
Server: I'll make a new one right away. It will take three minutes.
Customer: Thank you. May I also change my muffin to a plain one? I can't eat nuts.
Server: Of course. Actually, I'll give you the new drink for free.
Customer: That's very kind of you, but you don't have to.
Server: Please, it's the least we can do.
Customer: Well, thank you. I'll leave a tip, then.
Server: Thanks, that's very generous. Here's your order.

qs.q: What was wrong with the order?
o: The drink was coffee, not hot chocolate
The cup was the wrong size
qs.why: 손님은 핫초코를 주문했는데 커피처럼 보인다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can we guess about the first muffin?
o: It may have had nuts in it
qs.why: 손님이 'I can't eat nuts'라며 플레인 머핀으로 바꿔 달라고 했으므로 처음 머핀에는 견과류가 들어 있었을 거예요.

qs.q: What does "it's the least we can do" mean?
o: We want to do at least this to say sorry
We are not able to help
We can do nothing at all
qs.why: 사과의 뜻으로 최소한 이 정도는 해 드리고 싶다는 표현이에요.

qs.q: Why does the Customer mention the bus?
o: To show the order must be quick
To ask for a bus ticket
qs.why: 버스가 12분 뒤에 떠난다고 말하며 빨리 준비해 달라는 뜻을 간접적으로 전해요.

qs.q: What will the Customer probably do next?
o: Leave a tip and take the order
qs.why: 손님이 'I'll leave a tip, then'이라고 말하고 직원이 주문 음식을 건네요.

items.title: Bus to the Museum
items.text:
Yeji: I found a bus to the history museum. It leaves from the station at ten.
Chris: How long is the ride?
Yeji: About forty minutes. We'd arrive around ten forty.
Chris: Perfect. Is it free for students?
Yeji: Almost. Students pay only two thousand won with a student ID.
Chris: Oh, I left my ID in my old bag. I'd better find it.
Yeji: Please don't forget. Also, the museum closes at five, so we should leave by three-thirty.
Chris: Should we bring lunch, or eat there?
Yeji: There's a small cafe, but it's usually crowded. I'd rather bring sandwiches.
Chris: I agree. I'll make egg sandwiches tonight.

qs.q: How much do students pay with an ID?
qs.why: Yeji는 'Students pay only two thousand won with a student ID'라고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the museum cafe?
qs.why: 'usually crowded'는 사람이 많이 붐빈다는 뜻이므로 자주 손님이 많다고 볼 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "I'd rather bring sandwiches" mean?
qs.why: 'would rather'는 '차라리 ~하고 싶다, ~를 더 선호한다'는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Yeji say, "Please don't forget"?
o: To remind Chris about the ID
To warn Chris about the cafe
To ask Chris to buy tickets
To tell Chris to leave early
qs.why: 바로 앞에서 Chris가 학생증을 찾아야 한다고 말했어요. 잊지 말라는 당부예요.

qs.q: What will Chris probably do tonight?
qs.why: Chris는 'I'll make egg sandwiches tonight'라고 말해요.

items.title: A Mix-Up About the Deadline
items.text:
Lena: Sam, did you finish the English essay?
Sam: Not yet. The deadline is next month, so I have plenty of time.
Lena: Next month? I thought it was due tomorrow.
Sam: Mr. Park wrote "Friday, the 20th" on the board. I assumed that meant next month.
Lena: No, it means this month. Tomorrow is Friday the 20th.
Sam: Oh no! I haven't even started.
Lena: Why don't you ask Mr. Park for one more day?
Sam: Would he really agree?
Lena: He might, if you explain honestly. He gave Jisu extra time last week.
Sam: Okay, I'll talk to him before class. Can I see your outline?
Lena: Sure, but use it only for ideas.

qs.q: What did Mr. Park write on the board?
qs.why: Sam은 'Mr. Park wrote "Friday, the 20th" on the board'라고 말해요.

qs.q: How does Sam probably feel after learning the real deadline?
qs.why: Sam은 'Oh no! I haven't even started'라고 해요. 아직 시작도 안 해서 걱정돼요.

qs.q: What does "plenty of time" mean?
qs.why: 'plenty of'는 충분히 많은이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Lena say, "use it only for ideas"?
o: To tell Sam not to copy it
To say the outline is wrong
qs.why: 개요는 아이디어를 얻는 데에만 쓰라는 말로, 그대로 베끼지 말라는 의도예요.

qs.q: What will Sam probably do before class?
qs.why: Sam은 'I'll talk to him before class'라고 말하고, him은 Mr. Park이에요.

items.title: The New Lunch Menu
items.text:
Ji: What do you think of the new lunch menu?
Ben: Honestly, I like the vegetable soup, but the portions are small.
Ji: I agree. I'm still hungry after lunch.
Ben: Maybe we should tell the student council.
Ji: Do you think they would listen?
Ben: I do. Last year students asked for more fruit, and the school added apples twice a week.
Ji: That's encouraging. What should we say?
Ben: We could write a short letter and collect signatures.
Ji: Good idea. I'll ask our class today, and you can ask the next class.
Ben: Deal. Let's meet after school to count the names.

qs.q: What does Ben like about the new menu?
qs.why: Ben은 'I like the vegetable soup'라고 말해요. 양은 적다고 불평해요.

qs.q: What does the story about apples suggest?
o: Student requests can lead to change
qs.why: 학생들이 과일을 요청하자 학교가 사과를 추가했다는 이야기는 요청이 변화를 만들 수 있음을 보여줘요.

qs.q: What does "portions" mean?
qs.why: 'portion'은 한 사람에게 나오는 음식의 양을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why does Ji ask, "Do you think they would listen?"
o: To show some doubt about the plan
qs.why: Ji는 학생회가 들어줄지 확신하지 못해 의문을 나타내요. Ben이 사과 이야기를 하며 안심시켜요.

qs.q: What will Ji probably do today?
o: Ask the class to sign the letter
qs.why: Ji는 'I'll ask our class today'라고 하고 편지에 서명을 모으자는 계획이었어요.

items.title: Learning the Tablet
items.text:
Volunteer: Hello! Are you here for the tablet class?
Visitor: Yes, but I'm a little nervous. I've never used one.
Volunteer: Don't worry. We'll start with the basics. First, press this button to turn it on.
Visitor: Like this? Oh, it's much lighter than I thought.
Volunteer: Yes. Now touch the picture of the camera.
Visitor: Can I take a photo of my garden with it?
Volunteer: Absolutely. And you can send it to your friends by message.
Visitor: That would be wonderful. My friends live far away, and I miss them.
Volunteer: Then let's practise sending messages today. I'll sit beside you in case you get stuck.
Visitor: Thank you. You are very patient.

qs.q: What surprised the Visitor about the tablet?
qs.why: Visitor는 'it's much lighter than I thought'라고 말해요.

qs.q: What can we guess about the Visitor?
qs.why: Visitor는 'my garden'이라고 말하므로 정원이 있어요. 친구들은 멀리 살아요.

qs.q: What does "get stuck" mean?
qs.why: 'get stuck'은 막혀서 더 이상 진행하지 못하는 상황을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why does the Volunteer say, "Don't worry"?
qs.why: 방문객이 긴장된다고 말하자 안심시키려고 해요.

qs.q: What will the two probably do next?
qs.why: Volunteer가 'let's practise sending messages today'라고 말해요.

items.title: Which Platform?
items.text:
Traveler: Excuse me, my ticket says Platform 3, but a train just left from Platform 5.
Staff: Let me see your ticket. Ah, this ticket is for the 2:45 train, not the 2:15 train.
Traveler: Oh! I didn't notice the time. So I haven't missed it?
Staff: No. The 2:45 train will arrive on Platform 3 in about twenty minutes.
Traveler: What a relief! I thought I'd be late for an important interview.
Staff: You have time to get a drink. The kiosk is right behind you.
Traveler: Good idea. Which side?
Staff: Next to the stairs, on your left.
Traveler: Thank you for your help.
Staff: My pleasure. Please listen for announcements in case of changes.

qs.q: Which platform will the Traveler's train use?
qs.why: 직원은 2시 45분 열차가 3번 승강장에 들어온다고 말해요.

qs.q: Why was the Traveler worried?
o: A train had just left and the time was not checked
qs.why: 승객은 다른 열차가 막 떠난 것을 보고 놓쳤다고 생각했지만 표의 시간을 확인하지 않았어요.

qs.q: What does "What a relief!" mean?
o: The Traveler is glad the worry is gone
qs.why: 'What a relief!'는 걱정이 사라져 안심될 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

qs.q: Why does the Staff say, "Please listen for announcements in case of changes"?
o: To advise the Traveler to stay alert
To tell the Traveler to leave
qs.why: 일정이 바뀔 수 있으니 안내 방송을 주의해서 들으라고 조언하는 거예요.

qs.q: What will the Traveler probably do next?
o: Buy a drink at the kiosk
qs.why: 직원이 간이 매점을 알려 주었고 승객이 'Good idea'라고 답해요.
